hero_kpi_rationale: Service revenue is the central pillar of Deutsche Telekom's organic growth strategy and digital transformation, with strong exposure to cloud, fiber, and B2B digital services, notably through T-Systems.

kpis.name: Service Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from telecom and digital services (mobile, fixed-line, cloud, IoT).
kpis.description: Service revenue grew 2.9% in 2025, driven by fiber and digital services expansion in Germany and the United States.
kpis.signal: Stable growth despite market maturity, supported by fiber and cloud.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA AL (after lease)
kpis.explanation: Operating earnings before adjustment, excluding exceptional items and operating leases.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA AL reached 44.2 B€ in 2025, up 2.8%, driven by disciplined cost management and broadband growth.

kpis.name: Free Cash Flow (after lease)
kpis.explanation: Cash generated after capital investments, excluding dividends and spectrum.
kpis.description: FCF AL increased to 19.5 B€ in 2025, supported by EBITDA improvement and capex discipline.
kpis.signal: Cash generation capacity despite heavy infrastructure investments.

kpis.name: Capital expenditures (capex)
kpis.explanation: Infrastructure spending on network (fiber, 5G, data centers).
kpis.description: Capex totaled 19.3 B€ in 2025, slightly down, with focus on fiber and fixed networks.
kpis.signal: Capex stabilized after years of increases, indicating 5G deployment maturity.

kpis.name: Total net revenue
kpis.description: Net revenue reached 119.1 B€ in 2025, up 2.9%, driven by T-Mobile US and German fiber.
kpis.signal: Solid organic growth in a mature sector.

kpis.name: Total headcount
kpis.explanation: Full-time equivalent employees across the group.
kpis.description: The group had 198,000 employees in 2025, slightly down, with focus on digital productivity.

kpis.name: CO2 emissions (scopes 1 and 2)
kpis.explanation: Direct and energy-related group emissions (combustion and electricity consumption).
kpis.description: CO2 emissions declined to 240 kt in 2025, down 4.9%, thanks to energy efficiency and renewables.
kpis.signal: Continuous carbon footprint reduction, aligned with climate targets.

kpis.name: Dividends per share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 reported fiscal years by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $1.159 last year.

kpis.name: Capital returned (dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $6.438 billion last year.

kpis.name: Payout ratio
kpis.description: Payout ratio: Dividends paid / Net income, calculated over the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 67.0% last year.

kpis.name: Mobile customers
kpis.explanation: Total active mobile customers across the group.
kpis.description: Mobile customer count reached 205.5 million in 2025, up 4.5%, driven by U.S. acquisition strategy.
kpis.signal: Robust growth driven by T-Mobile US.

kpis.name: Revenue share in Germany
kpis.explanation: Proportion of total revenue generated in Germany.
kpis.description: German revenue share declined to 22.0% in 2025, reflecting faster T-Mobile US growth.
kpis.signal: Gradual geographic diversification toward international markets, notably T-Mobile US.

risks.title: Intense competitive pressure in European and U.S. telecom markets
risks.score_rationale: Implied through higher sales support provisions (EUR 623M in 2025, +EUR 0.1Bn) and rising reseller commissions, signaling active price competition. Trend shows increasing defensive commercial spending.

risks.title: Workforce transformation risk and restructuring costs
risks.score_rationale: The '2025 Workforce Transformation' program is explicitly cited, with severance provisions up EUR 0.2Bn. Language is direct ('centralizing executives', 'eliminating duplicate roles'), indicating significant restructuring underway.

risks.title: Dependency on public subsidies for broadband rollout
risks.score_rationale: Liabilities tied to publicly funded projects increased EUR 0.2Bn to EUR 1.557Bn, with deployment obligations conditioned on subsidy receipt. This regulatory and budget dependency risk is sector-specific.

risks.title: Regulatory risk related to civil servant status and pension obligations
risks.score_rationale: Obligations to the Civil Service Pension Fund (33% of emoluments) and PBeaKK represent multiyear commitments constrained by German public law. Annual contribution remains EUR 212M in 2025, with future obligations of EUR 0.4Bn.

risks.title: Acquisition integration and dilution risk from major deals (UScellular)
risks.score_rationale: UScellular acquisition cited multiple times as driver of higher provisions (restoration +EUR 0.2Bn, contracts +EUR 0.2Bn). Integrating an asset this size into T-Mobile US generates significant operational and financial risks.

risks.title: Shareholder dilution risk from T-Mobile US stake dispositions
risks.score_rationale: Minority shareholder transactions reduced equity by EUR 7.8Bn in 2025, mainly through T-Mobile US share buybacks and DT stake sales. Managing the T-Mobile US stake is a central strategic risk.

risks.title: Site restoration obligations and rising environmental costs
risks.score_rationale: Restoration obligations provisions reached EUR 1.755Bn (+EUR 0.1Bn in 2025), with scope impacts from UScellular. Language ('dismantling and removing assets, restoring sites') indicates long-term contractual environmental commitments.

risks.title: Material litigation risks linked to global operations
risks.score_rationale: Litigation provisions totaled EUR 623M at end-2025 (+EUR 0.1Bn vs. 2024), with EUR 585M in additions during the year. High level and upward trend indicate structural litigation exposure across multiple jurisdictions.

ai_positioning.summary: Deutsche Telekom is gradually integrating artificial intelligence into customer service and network operations, without being a technology leader. Focus is on automation and user experience improvement.
evidence: Deployment of AI tools for customer service (chatbots, voice support)
AI use for mobile network optimization and predictive maintenance
Partnerships with cloud providers for B2B solutions with AI capabilities
